analysis.title: S&P 500 Futures: What Stops the Selling?
key_insights: Non-Dealers sold $10.5bn of S&P 500 futures from September 22nd to 29th, the 5th week of selling in the past 6 since August 18th, for a net -$63.7bn. Shorts dominated the latest release, while long unwinds accounted for more than 70% of the selling across the 1.5 month window.
Asset Managers led the selling, with $11.7bn sold in the latest report and Other selling another $1.1bn. Hedge Funds bought $620mm and Non-Reportables bought $1.6bn.

Higher real rates and/or quarterly rebalancing weighed on positioning. Asset Manager liquidation was $5.5bn, coinciding with a 25bp jump in US 10 year real yields. The rolling 3 month correlation between Asset Manager gross longs and USGGT10Y Index moved well into negative territory.
Because the report is dated close to quarter-end, GS suggests general asset reallocation may have started early.

Lower probabilities of imminent Fed hikes lifted equities. A below-consensus PCE, dovish Fed speakers and a miss on Nonfarm payrolls reduced hike pricing for October, supporting a 0.70% recovery in the S&P index.
S&P futures flows arguably remained bearish because deferred real rates rose marginally. The December Adjusted Interest Rate future, used as a funding proxy, cheapened by about 5bps.
Asset Manager net length was at a 77% 2 year rank on September 29th, before counting additional probable sales. GS expects ongoing challenges for equities until yields convincingly reverse.
GS rates research sees recent developments and valuation as presenting a clearer skew toward lower yields, despite upward pressure from oil and resilient AI investment plans.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The below-consensus print, with dovish Fed speakers and the payrolls miss, reduced October Fed hike pricing and helped the S&P recover 0.70%.
The miss reduced pricing for an October Fed hike and supported equities.
The rise coincided with Asset Manager liquidation of $5.5bn in S&P futures.
Reduced hike pricing boosted equities, though deferred real rates rose marginally.

risk_factors: Real yields rising further, which would keep Asset Manager liquidation going.
Quarterly rebalancing and early asset reallocation near quarter-end.
Upward pressure on yields from oil and resilient AI investment plans.
A still elevated Asset Manager net position leaves room for more selling.

tension_points.bear_case: Deferred real rates rose marginally, Asset Manager net length is at a 77% 2 year rank with more sales probable, and oil and AI investment plans add upward pressure on yields.
